extracted.intended_audience: scientists and educated general readers (readers of Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative points used in Nature book reviews and short notices for judging scientific/technical books, reports, and institutional conduct. Covers content quality, evidence, presentation, production, and practical impact across subjects (dietetics, chemistry, engineering, natural history, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of dietary protein
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the protein is of the first importance; it must supply the particular amino-acids required by the consumer, and must supply them in the proper amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion led up to and illustrated by an account of pellagra; book devoted to quality of protein and practical consequences for choice of food.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and essentiality of vitamins
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be present the vitamins, the exact nature and function of which are still unknown, but which are essential for growth and health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors treat discovery and distribution of vitamins; appendices/tables listing vitamin distribution in food-stuffs are valuable for assessing diets; recent discoveries (e.g., sunlight and rickets) can change positions quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for fresh natural food-stuffs for safety
rubrics_metrics.description: The gospel preached ... that safety is to be found in fresh natural food-stuffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: white bread is inferior in vitaminic potency to whole‑meal/germ bread; green vegetables and salads are necessary; instinct is not a reliable guide under modern civilisation; distribution within family should consider actual nutritional needs of children vs wage-earners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Household food distribution should match nutritional needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The distribution of food within the family is often conducted on quite erroneous principles; children need protein and vitamins in addition to calories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of custom giving the best food to the father/wage-earner; stresses that children need growth nutrients, not just high-energy staples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonal/animal-diet variation in vitamin content
rubrics_metrics.description: Even natural food-stuffs are by no means constant in their content of vitamins; in products derived from animals this variation is still more marked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The milk of cows at grass contains more A-factor than the milk of the same cows on their winter food' — implication: breast-feeding is no protection against rickets if mother's food is poor in A-factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of preservation methods on vitamins
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief methods for the prolonged preservation of food are canning or bottling and drying, and a considerable amount of investigation has already been directed to the question how far these methods of treatment affect the vitamins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oxidation is important; drying often reduces antiscorbutic power (e.g., cabbage reduced to 5–10% on drying at 37°); heat sterilisation affects antiscorbutic vitamin more; some foods (canned tomatoes, lemon-juice with rind oil) retain potency — each case must be separately examined; need quantitative studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of preserved foods with retained vitamin potency
rubrics_metrics.description: There seems ... to be no insuperable difficulty in the way of the provision of preserved foods containing at all events a large proportion of their original vitaminic potency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimistic note: methods may be found to retain/enrich vitamins in cheap edible oils; further investigation required on quantitative lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Altruistic management and licensing policy of a chemical foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of a foundation: privately managed enterprise, well-known men of high character as voting trustees, president not salaried, non‑exclusive licences granted to break monopolies, licences to Government free, low royalties on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such policies illustrated by claimed fall in medicine prices (e.g., salvarsan) and argued as evidence of benefit to consumers; used to judge whether sale price was fair competitive price rather than nominal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive vs monopoly‑based price assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the original price paid by the Foundation for the patents may have been 'nearly a nominal sum' if regarded as a monopoly price, it was nevertheless a fair competitive price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance based on observed effect on prices to physicians and government purchasers; use market-price evidence to judge fairness of transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of advisory/representative committees matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Action is being taken by the American Chemical Society ... through a committee which does not include dye-makers or chemical manufacturers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied criterion: whether stakeholders are included affects persuasiveness and completeness of information presented to policymakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: County geography should include index and correlate distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Asserts that county geography series should include more correlation of various distributions and causal effects; criticises omission of index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: maps stopping at county boundaries reduce usefulness; omission of causal effects weakens geographic treatment of population distribution and town sites; an index and broader map coverage improve utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise works should avoid extreme brevity in key diagnostic descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A synoptical list that uses extreme brevity in descriptions (diagnostic characters restricted to adult plumages, leaving immature stages untouched) is of limited use to general students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A useful synopsis needs fuller descriptions including immature stages and fuller treatment of geographical ranges; authors urged to produce monographs dealing with plumages, distribution, and life-histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of a useful ornithological life-history entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the description of each bird there should be sections devoted to habits, nesting, eggs, young, plumages, food, behaviour, and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhance with plates: coloured plates of eggs and photographic plates of breeding colonies and young; inclusion of coloured figures of adult birds is desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria justifying railway electrification
rubrics_metrics.description: Electrification is justified when it provides increased transport facilities with no increase in the rates; historically used where abnormal difficulties (long tunnels, busy urban traffic, steep gradients, high fuel price) existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider central power generation vs individual power, risk of wide-area breakdown requiring stand-by plant, capital costs, potential to purchase bulk supply, and comparative running-cost accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair accounting comparison of electric vs steam locomotives
rubrics_metrics.description: Electric locomotive takes power only when running and requires less time for maintenance; experience shows fewer electric locomotives required for a given service, but each electric must bear its share of central station working costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To compare fairly, include share of central station costs in the electric system's accounting; don't ignore overheads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical origins of poor locomotive riding qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Bad riding qualities are due to (1) the constraint of the wheels to follow other courses than those towards which they naturally tend, and (2) resonant oscillations under the control of the springs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phenomena: 'nosing' and 'rearing' ascribed to wheel constraint, 'rolling' and 'pitching' to resonant oscillations; dynamical analysis can guide engineering improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardisation choices in railway electrification systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory committee decided in favour of the direct current system, with a line pressure of 1500 volts, though multiples or submultiples may be used; single‑phase and polyphase advocates exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences in cost between systems are small (about 1–2% of total running cost); while standardisation is desirable, multiple systems have been adopted historically; practitioners should weigh national and operational considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineering manual usefulness: practical explanation and exhaustive conversion material
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric system manual aimed at those who use millimetre in practice but lack confidence in calculating with metric units — should explain the system and state in full how to convert between English and metric units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exhaustive conversion tables, account of measurement devices (vernier), and practical argumentation (not mere propaganda) to persuade conservative audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical criteria for school physics textbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanise elementary physics without popularising it: theory should have main prominence; experiments described only to elucidate principles; frequent references to makers of scientific history; connect pupil's own experience with principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include interesting plates (portraits of Newton, Pascal, Boyle, Galileo, Joseph Black); structure could treat mechanics/hydrostatics and heat in accessible order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical manual currency and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Third edition called for because material has been appreciated; revision brings tables of constants into accord with best data; include accounts of recent important work (e.g., X‑ray spectra, positive rays, atomic structure theories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A systematic account of latest developments, updated constants, and inclusion of recent landmark work make a manual recommendable to readers seeking up-to-date understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthropological/ethnographic work should avoid author prejudice
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnographic accounts useful when written with sympathy and care; prejudice that stigmatizes customs (calling them 'degrading', 'disgusting') reduces impartiality and usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect folklore and describe practices (e.g., fetish societies) carefully; where prejudice affects narrative, readers may require additional knowledge to disentangle facts from bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book production and illustration as evaluative factors
rubrics_metrics.description: A book that is well produced and contains a number of interesting illustrations, appendices with useful tables and notes, aids rapid assessment and dissemination of sound doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: appendices giving tables of vitamin distribution and lists of food-stuffs rich in each vitamin provide quick practical utility; coloured maps and plates enhance the usability of geographical and natural-history texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical/scientific appreciation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To appraise a scientist (e.g., Francis Galton) consider breadth of training, originality (first correlation table, first regression curve), experimental testing, and influence on subsequent fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualise contributions in the epoch (Victorian science), note foundational innovations (correlational calculus, heredity measures), and balance 'nature' and 'nurture' discussions with modern perspectives.
